title: Authorization traffic controller and audit streamer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a production-ready authorization traffic controller (ATC) that centralizes policy evaluation across API, runtime, and Console surfaces, and an audit streamer that reliably ships allow/deny decisions and contextual metadata to downstream sinks. The ATC will: 1) accept authorization queries from edge proxies and internal services, 2) perform fast policy evaluation against RBAC v2 rules, attribute sets (including SAML/SSO-mapped groups), and session context, 3) return decision + explanation + TTL for caching, and 4) optionally perform soft-fail fallbacks (allow/deny with telemetry) based on operator policy. The audit streamer will: 1) fan out audit events to Kafka and internal audit-sink (for SOC/Compliance), 2) include immutable request context (request id, principal, role bindings, evaluated rule id, dataset hash), and 3) support batching, backpressure and replay for late consumers. Scope excludes long-term storage retention policy (handled by compliance team) and UI for admin controls (separate Console ticket). This ticket implements runtime components, evaluation caching layer, SAML attribute mapping hooks, and the audit streaming pipeline integration.
acceptance_criteria: ATC responds to authz queries within 15ms p95 for simple lookups (cached) and 60ms p95 for uncached complex rules in our benchmark cluster
Decision responses include explained_rule_id, evaluated_attributes, decision_ttl and correlation_id
Audit streamer emits structured events to Kafka topic redwood.audit.authz-v2 and a parallel low-latency HTTP sink for SOC
SAML/SSO attribute mappings can be loaded dynamically from config and are used in evaluation in staging
Feature flags allow operator to switch ATC between strict (deny on error) and permissive (allow on error + telemetry) modes
End-to-end tests cover API->ATC->audit-sink with simulated Kafka backpressure and ensure no data loss beyond configured retry policy
